paragraphs: The hardware implementation of the moisture sensor system was thoroughly tested to ensure its accuracy, reliability, and compliance with operational specifications. The testing methodology involved several key steps, including the execution of predefined test cases under various conditions.

For TC_01: Dry Soil Alert Test, the system was set up in a dry environment with a moisture level below 30%. The expected behavior was for the Buzzer to be active (HIGH) and the Status LED PC13 to be turned on (LOW). Upon execution, the observed response matched the expected outcome, confirming that the system functioned as intended.

For TC_02: Optimal Moisture Inactive Test, the system was set up in an optimal environment with a moisture level between 30% and 80%. The expected behavior was for the Buzzer to be inactive (LOW) and the Status LED PC13 to be turned on (HIGH). Upon execution, the observed response matched the expected outcome, validating that the system functioned as intended.

For TC_03: Excess Moisture / Saturated Test, the system was set up in an excessively wet environment with a moisture level above 80%. The expected behavior was for the Buzzer to be inactive (LOW) and the Status LED PC13 to be turned on (HIGH). Upon execution, the observed response matched the expected outcome, confirming that the system functioned as intended.

The operational boundaries of the system were also verified. The system was tested under conditions where moisture levels were below 30%, between 30% and 80%, and above 80%. The results showed that the system accurately captured moisture levels within these ranges, with no significant deviation from expected behavior.

The mathematical stability of the system was also analyzed. The system was tested under various conditions to ensure that it maintained its performance over time. The results showed that the system remained stable and accurate, with no noticeable degradation in performance over time.
